title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: US envoy Witkoff arrives for Putin talks
preheader: Europe weighs a Donbas-for-NATO idea as an Abyei strike kills dozens.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, October 21, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: US envoy Witkoff arrives in St Petersburg to meet Putin
stories.why_important: Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Vladimir Putin on the war. European leaders are debating their own talks with the Kremlin; the Financial Times reports one idea: Russia keeps the Donbas and Ukraine gets NATO membership. Trump again said Ukraine must want a deal.
stories.what_overlooked: The idea that Russia keeps the Donbas and Ukraine joins NATO comes from a Financial Times columnist. That writer described what European politicians now say privately, but no government has confirmed it as policy.
stories.prediction: A joint statement or a follow-up meeting after Witkoff's St Petersburg talks would show whether Washington is negotiating terms or only listening.

stories.story_title: Drone strike on Abyei market kills at least 53, officials say
stories.why_important: A drone hit Amiet market in Abyei, a region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan, on Monday, starting a fire at a fuel depot. Local officials count 53 to 153 dead and blame Sudan's army; a Sudanese officer said the army carried out the strike.
stories.what_overlooked: South Sudan's 2011 independence left Abyei's status unresolved, and the market attack hit civilians in a zone where both armies operate.
stories.prediction: A confirmed toll and any Sudanese army statement in 72 hours will show whether the strike becomes a dispute between Khartoum and Juba.

stories.story_title: Nigeria records first Ebola case as outbreak spreads
stories.why_important: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case on Tuesday, in a patient who arrived from Uganda, and Kenya declared a ninth case. The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May, and it has now spread across several countries. Nigeria's size and travel links make it harder to contain the virus.
stories.what_overlooked: Uganda's health ministry said it has no active Ebola cases, even as its neighbor confirmed an infection in a traveler who came from there.
stories.prediction: Whether Nigeria reports more cases by Friday will show if the virus is spreading inside Africa's most populous country or border officials caught it.

quick_hits.text: Elon Musk ordered SpaceX to cap Starlink speeds for Ukraine's military last week, the Wall Street Journal reports, disrupting drone operations.
Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX and Tesla are discussing a merger that would create a company worth about $3.5 trillion.
Botswana's energy regulator said a bill creating power trading and private transmission lines goes to Parliament in November.
The Financial Times reported that Trump opposed Netanyahu's plan for early October strikes on Iran's power plants and nuclear sites.
Iran's security chief told Pakistan's army chief that no enriched nuclear material will leave the country, state television reported.
A Russian jailed over anti-war posts says Lithuanian border guards refused to let him request asylum after he swam the Neman River.
